summary: Elevated 5xx rate from API gateway after mixed embedding + chat burst causing runtime GPU resets
description: Issue summary: Customer (NovaChat Inc.) reported an increase in 5xx responses on their dedicated tenant beginning ~2026-03-13T18:05Z. Errors were concentrated on the /v1/embeddings and /v1/chat/stream endpoints and correlated with a simultaneous heavy embedding upload + live chat traffic spike.
impact: Multiple production clients observed token-generation failures and stream disconnects. Aggregate 5xx rate for the tenant rose to ~18% during the peak window (18:05Z-18:28Z). Tail latency increased (p95 from 420ms to ~3.6s). Several upstream runtime pods restarted due to NVML driver resets, causing additional request amplification and a sustained elevated error floor.
environment_details: Dedicated pool: dp-wn-02 (4 x A100s), autoscaler policy: conservative node add (cooldown 120s), apigw config: keepalive 60s, max-connections-per-worker 1024. Tenant traffic mix: concurrent small chat (low-token) streams + large embedding batches (single request sizes up to 10k sparse vectors).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Submit multiple concurrently interleaved requests: many small streaming chat sessions (20-50 rps) AND a few large embedding uploads (2-4 requests with 5k-10k vectors) from the same tenant. 2) Observe apigw connection churn and burst in accept queue. 3) Verify kvcache eviction & runtime GPU memory allocation spikes. 4) Watch for NVML reset events in runtime logs and subsequent 5xx responses from upstream.
logs_and_metrics_summary:
- Apigw logs (18:05Z): accept_queue_wait > 2s, connection resets up 4x baseline.
- Error rate: 5xx jumped from 0.6% baseline to 18% at peak.
- Runtime logs: repeated NVML_ERROR: device is lost + kernel abort messages; container restarts 6 times across three nodes.
- GPU telemetry: sustained 98% memory utilization, occasional driver OOMs and ECC errors flagged.
- kvcache: eviction rate spike and lock contention metrics increased during the same window.
- Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/tenant/tenant-dp-wn-02?from=2026-03-13T18:00Z&to=2026-03-13T18:30Z
timeline:
- 18:03Z: NovaChat schedules large embedding preprocess job.
- 18:05Z: Apigw accept-queue grows; first 5xx observed.
- 18:07Z: Runtime reports NVML reset on node worker-03; worker restarts.
- 18:11Z: Autoscaler attempts node add but cooldown prevents immediate recovery.
- 18:18Z: We applied temporary tenant rate limit to embedding endpoints. 5xx rate begins to decline.
- 18:25Z: Additional runtime restarts observed after another embedding chunk completed.
- 18:28Z: Error rate settles to ~1.2% after blocking large uploads and scaling dedicated pool by +2 nodes.
initial_investigation_notes: Hypothesis: concurrent mixed workload (many long-lived streaming connections + large embedding uploads) caused connection thrashing at apigw leading to hot spots in the accept queue and amplified retries. Upstream runtimes experienced rapid memory allocations and NVML driver contention, triggering device resets. Lock contention in kvcache prefetch paths increased GC and eviction activity, contributing to runtime instability.
actions_taken:
- Immediately applied tenant-level soft rate limit on /v1/embeddings for NovaChat.
- Temporarily disabled aggressive short-circuit retries on apigw for streaming routes.
- Scaled the customer's dedicated pool by adding 2 nodes (manual override).
- Notified SRE on-call and opened runtime hotfix PR to add defensive NVML reset handling.
- Customer notified with mitigation steps and temporary workaround (stagger embedding uploads).

root_cause: Combination of apigw accept-queue saturation from connection churn (mixed long-lived streams + large embeddings) and upstream runtime GPU driver instability under immediate high-allocation pressure. The autoscaler cooldown and conservative add policy delayed capacity recovery, allowing retries and restarts to amplify the failure.
resolution_summary: Temporary mitigation: tenant embedding rate-limited and dedicated pool manually scaled; streaming retry policy adjusted. Customer workaround: stagger embedding uploads and reduce per-request vector counts. Engineering PR opened to improve NVML reset handling and add admission control to reject expensive embedding uploads during streaming bursts.
long_term_fix_plan: Merge runtime PR to catch and gracefully handle NVML resets + reduce automatic hard restarts (PR #2523)
Add admission-control / cost-estimate step in apigw to reject or queue large embedding uploads when a tenant has active streaming sessions
Tune autoscaler policy for dedicated pools: reduce cooldown for emergency scale-adds and add burst-mode override for P1 tenants
Investigate kvcache prefetch lock contention and add per-tenant prefetch throttling
Create a tenant-level best-practices doc for mixed workloads (confluence page draft)
Improve observability: synthetic mixed-workload load tests and alerting on accept-queue latency > 500ms for >2m
